thread.title: The Milwaukee-area stocks pummeled in the market rout

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: The Milwaukee-area stocks pummeled in the market rout
text: – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Feb 6, 2018, 2:37pm CST Stock markets appeared to ease somewhat today following a record-setting selloff Feb. 5 that sent shockwaves throughout the U.S. economy. But even after rebounding from early losses this morning, major stock indices continued to waver from positive to negative territory throughout much of the day. Wall Street experts said the broader declines, which began in earnest Jan. 29, might be driven by investor worries that the economy is entering a period of steeper than normal inflation. The recent losses have been widespread and industry agnostic. Among the biggest losers as of Monday was Seattle-based radio technology and software maker Impinj Inc. (Nasdaq: PI), which saw its stock price plummet 45 percent to $11.94 between Jan. 29 and Feb. 5. Other companies that took double-digit hits to their stock prices included Overstock.com (Nasdaq: OSTK), down 36 percent to $49.50; Eastman Kodak Co. (NYSE: KODK) down 35 percent to $6.20; and Bellicum Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: BLCM) down 35 percent to $5.61. Following those national players was one company with Milwaukee-area ties: Roadrunner transportation Systems Inc., formerly based in Cudahy. Downers Grove, Ill.-based Roadrunner (Nasdaq: RRTS), which still has Milwaukee-area operations, closed down 32 percent Monday from Jan. 29. Other Milwaukee-area stocks that got hit this past week include Glendale-based Strattec Security Corp. (NYSE: STRT) and The Manitowoc Co. Inc. (NYSE: MTW), which is relocating its headquarters to Milwaukee, both down 17 percent, Milwaukee-based Harley-Davidson Inc. (NYSE: HOG) down 16 percent, and Sussex-based Quad/Graphics Inc. (NYSE: QUAD), Menomonee Falls-based Actuant Corp. (NYSE: ATU) and Milwaukee-based ManpowerGroup Inc. (NYSE: MAN) all down 13 percent. The slide follows a stretch that saw U.S. stocks hit historic highs amid investor excitement over strong corporate earnings reports, a growing economy and the passage of a business-friendly tax bill. Last month, the stalwart Dow Jones Industrial Average took just seven days to add 1,000 points and surpass 26,000 for the first time in its history. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 also set new records in the early days of 2018. Markets took a sharp turn last week, and the declines accelerated through Monday, with the Dow tumbling to a low of 24,085 as of Tuesday's opening bell. Gina Martin Adams , chief equity strategist for Bloomberg Intelligence, said investors were overly optimistic in 2017 amid a steady stream of strong corporate earnings reports. But a number of sectors have been rocked by developments that created something of a contagion effect heading into this week's selloff, Adams said. For example, health care stocks spiraled in the wake of the joint announcement by Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN), Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) and JPMorgan Chase (NYSEL: JPM) of plans to create a joint health care venture aimed at reducing health care costs for employees. Similar reverberations hit the tech sector with Apple’s (Nasdaq: AAPL) introduction of an update to its health app that will enable customers to view medical records on their phones. Add in disappointing earnings reports from ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) and Chevron (NYSE: CVX), and some investors are feeling the heat, spurring fears that ultimately rippled through the broader market, Adams said. “There were some pretty big losses in some specialized products,” Adams said. “It seems to be a symptom of a deflation of the excess of investor optimism." “It’s still a bull market,” Adams said. “As long as the fundamentals of the market are strong, which they are, I don’t see that changing.” – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Feb 6, 2018, 2:37pm CST
